history.origins: Tuong (Tướng) belongs to Vietnam's national climbing-card tradition. The closely related game Tiến Lên (Go Forward) is considered the national card game of Vietnam and shares the same shedding-and-climbing family as Zheng Shangyou and President. The genre spread beyond Vietnam, including to the USA after the Vietnam War where it is sometimes known as Thirteen or Viet Cong.
timeline: 20th century: National card game of Vietnam; part of climbing game family (Tiến Lên).
history.evolution: Part of the Climbing game family (cf. President, Dai Hinmin).

rules.objective: Be the first to shed all cards from your hand; the last player with cards loses the round.
rules.gameplay: Play single/pair/triple/straight/double-sequence. Must match type and beat previous play. Pass if can't/won't. Bombs beat 2s: Four-of-a-kind beats single 2. Long double-sequences beat pairs of 2s. Round ends when all pass; winner starts new round.

strategy.basic: Play low cards early. Save 2s for late.
strategy.advanced: Count cards. Trap opponents with bomb timing.

variations.name: No twos in sequences

variations.description: When all but one have passed, the last player to play may continue with successively higher combinations of the same type until unable.

scoring.description: First out wins. Remaining players ranked by cards left.
